_note: Protocol = the paper's R code with deviation D5 in docs/paper-replication.md: each node fits on its own, so the plateau rule acts on each node's validation NLL, not on the summed one. The Bernstein domain is the reference's train min/max (range_q 0), as in CAREFL. Paper Sec. 5.1-5.2. The interventional means are analytic (E[x3|do(x2=a)] = -0.25 + 0.25a), so the check is the flow's error against them, not a pinned flow value. do(x2=-3) is off-manifold extrapolation. The do(x2) errors are seed-sensitive; docs/paper-replication.md holds the spread over init seeds. Pinned at the reference's own 10000 epochs @ lr 0.001 with the per-node plateau rule; bounds sit at 1.5x to 4x the pinned measurement.

fit_seconds.why: 3x the 2-core CI runner measurement (436.8 s, the reference 10000-epoch plateau protocol): shared-runner wall clock is noisy, so this is a gross-regression tripwire, not a benchmark
